rounds.proof_sketch: With dim2=256 and blockDim.x=256, blockDim.z=1: Original=(256+256-1)/256=1, Mutated=(256+1-1)/256=1. Both equal 1 because dim2 is exactly divisible by blockDim.x. The mutation converts ceiling to floor division, but these are identical when dim2 % blockDim.x = 0.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the ceiling division formula `(dim2 + blockDim.x - 1) / blockDim.x` to effectively floor division `dim2 / blockDim.x` by replacing blockDim.x (256) with blockDim.z (1) in the numerator adjustment. However, with the fixed shape having dim2=256 and the hardcoded block_size=256, both expressions evaluate to exactly 1. Ceiling and floor division only differ when there's a remainder, but 256/256 has no remainder. This makes the mutation semantically equivalent for this specific configuration regardless of tensor values.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. Would require dim2 to not be a multiple of 256 (e.g., dim2=257 would yield original=2 vs mutated=1, causing elements 256+ to be missed).
rounds.recommendations: When testing max-reduction kernels, include dimension sizes that are NOT exact multiples of the block size to expose off-by-one errors in work distribution calculations. The current test shape [16, 256, 256] with block_size=256 creates a degenerate case where ceiling and floor division are equivalent.
